open_issues.next: fix at the cleanup of the phase; fix idea: In packages/orch/lib/orch/conductor/infrastructure/lease.py, let FileLock open with O_RDONLY when it is used for probing (create=False), because flock works on a read-only descriptor and the samestat check stays valid. Also make probe_free treat an EACCES or EROFS on open as 'cannot prove free' and return False, so status keeps showing 'running' and never traces back. Regression check: add a test to packages/orch/tests/test_run_lease.py that chmods lease.lock to 0o444 (and covers a held lock). It asserts probe_free returns True when the lock is free and False when it is held, and that effective_status does not raise.
open_issues.text: deferred minor finding packages/orch/lib/orch/conductor/infrastructure/lease.py:31: probe_free (used by runs.effective_status for `conduct status`, `status --json`, `runs`) opens lease.lock with O_RDWR outside the try that only wraps flock. In a read-only context (a role running under ro-run/Landlock or a codex read-only sandbox, or a read-only mount) the open fails with EACCES/EROFS, and the PermissionError/OSError escapes probe_free, so `orch conduct status --run <live run>` exits with a traceback instead of printing `running`. This happens exactly when a run is live (journal running + run.json lease:true), so a read-only role that inspects the run it belongs to crashes the command. flock works on an O_RDONLY descriptor, so the probe needs no write access.
